strategy.summary: Reproduce GH-63278 (recoverable OverflowError during Period construction from an extremely negative Timestamp at microsecond resolution) by running pandas’ Period construction test that uses `Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit="us")` and `Period(ts, freq="us")`. The buggy revision should raise `OverflowError` during Period conversion, while the fixed revision should construct `per` without propagating the overflow and allow the test’s property assertions to pass.

build_commands: python -m pip install -U pip setuptools wheel
pinned_because: No explicit NumPy/Python version constraints are provided in the evidence. To maximize the chance of matching the C-extension codepath that triggers the `np_datetime.c` overflow, use the same dependency set as pandas’ source build requirements (NumPy + Cython), but leave versions unpinned unless your CI pins them elsewhere.

strategy.reproducing_test:
def test_construction_from_min_timestamp(self):
    # GH-63278
    ts = Timestamp(Timestamp.min.value, unit="us")
    per = Period(ts, freq="us")

    # pandas.errors.OutOfBoundsDatetime: Out of bounds nanosecond timestamp:
    # -290308-12-21 19:59:05
    # rt = per.to_timestamp()

    assert per.year == ts.year
    assert per.month == ts.month
    assert per.day == ts.day
    assert per.hour == ts.hour
    assert per.minute == ts.minute
    assert per.second == ts.second
strategy.success_criterion: On the buggy pandas revision (commit 73e3149d1311), the statement `per = Period(ts, freq="us")` (or the internal conversion it triggers) propagates an `OverflowError` (recoverable overflow bug), causing the test to fail before the `assert per.*` lines. On the fixed revision (the PR that implements the overflow-checked split arithmetic for microsecond scaling), `Period(ts, freq="us")` succeeds and all `per.{year,month,day,hour,minute,second} == ts.{...}` assertions pass.
strategy.numerical_probe: The failure is in the seconds→microseconds scaling used during Period construction from a near-minimum Timestamp at `unit="us"`: it multiplies an extremely negative seconds value (discussion notes `seconds = -9223372036855`) by `10**6`, overflowing in `scaleSecondsToMicroseconds`, and previously didn’t properly recover from the overflow.

risks: Version sensitivity: because the evidence does not specify an exact NumPy version, the precise overflow behavior/stack may vary with toolchain and NumPy’s vendored datetime internals. However, the test’s transition is still based on whether the OverflowError propagates during `Period(ts, freq="us")` in pandas’ C-extension codepath.

Platform/toolchain sensitivity: the exception location references `np_datetime.c:458` within pandas’ vendored/linked code. That line number can shift across builds/compilers even if the underlying overflow condition remains.

Architecture/sanitizer differences: if the bug only manifests under certain architectures or when particular integer overflow handling occurs, the transition might not reproduce on all environments. No such constraint is documented in the evidence, so this risk is speculative but real.
Window/Emscripten dependency (`tzdata`) is only required on those platforms; the evidence says it is not numerically relevant elsewhere, so avoid installing it unless you are on Windows/Emscripten.

oracle.reference_source: The “oracle” is the test itself: successful construction of `per` without propagating the OverflowError, followed by equality of individual date-time fields between `per` and `ts`. The evidence does not specify a numeric tolerance or a reference computed value.
oracle.why: The reproduced test does not compare the overflowed/scaled integer directly; it only checks that `per` fields match `ts` fields after construction, so passing/failing is binary based on whether the conversion completes without error.

strategy.fails_on_buggy: The assertion framework will observe failure because `per = Period(ts, freq="us")` raises `OverflowError` during Period conversion; this prevents reaching the `assert per.year == ts.year` and the test fails.
strategy.passes_on_fixed: `Period(ts, freq="us")` completes without propagating the overflow (recoverable overflow is handled via overflow-checked split arithmetic), and the `per.year/month/day/hour/minute/second` assertions all pass.
